dossier.valuation_method: Multi-stage book-value-per-share compounding at a probability-weighted sustainable ROE (financial/spread frame), discounted at 14.8% cost of equity; terminal P/B reconciled to warranted (ROE-g)/(CoE-g); cross-checked with normalized earnings power and peer P/B-vs-ROE.
dossier.thesis_summary: Root is a recently-profitable telematics auto insurer that genuinely fixed its underwriting (gross loss ratio ~82%->59%), wound down quota-share reinsurance, and grows fast (revenue $455M FY23->$1.52B FY25; first profit FY24-25). Three years of accelerating FAVORABLE reserve development (-$7.0M/-$19.4M/-$29.4M) confirm the turn is real and conservatively reserved. As a financial/spread business it is valued on book compounding at a sustainable ROE: common book ~$18.4/share FD, ROE ~16% through cycle (cyclically higher). It is the best insurtech underwriter but sub-scale (0.4% share) vs incumbents with permanent cost-of-capital advantages, runs high ~3.3-5x premium-to-surplus leverage, and has undisclosed/high churn. Probability-weighted FMV ~$25, floor ~$20 (1.1x book), with 30% weight on a ~$40 compounder outcome and 28% on cycle/competitive/leverage impairment.
key_value_drivers: Sustainable through-cycle ROE / book-value compounding rate (the dominant driver)
Durability of the ~59% gross loss ratio (and accident-year vs development-aided calendar loss ratio) as the cycle softens
PIF/premium growth from embedded (Carvana) + independent-agent channels, state expansion, and retention
Terminal P/B (a function of terminal ROE vs cost of equity as Root de-risks)
Investment-yield redeployment from cash-heavy 3.4% toward ~5% (+$6-8M/yr) and operating leverage
key_risks: Loss-ratio edge unproven through a full soft cycle; ~2pts of 2025 calendar loss ratio aided by favorable prior-year development
High premium-to-surplus (~3.3-5x net), risen as quota share wound down - thin cushion for a bad accident year
Undisclosed retention; high-churn model requires heavy new business to grow PIF (implied 1-yr retention ~70-80%)
Sub-scale (0.4% share) vs float-funded incumbents with ~50x ad budgets and lower cost of capital
Carvana concentration (~19.3% as-converted owner/partner); warrant overhang dilutive only at much higher prices
what_would_change_my_mind: Net combined ratio sustained above 100% or gross loss ratio drifting above the 65% target
A reversal from favorable to adverse prior-year reserve development
Disclosure of weak/declining retention undermining LTV/CAC
Conversely: sustained PIF re-acceleration at target loss ratio + portfolio-yield redeployment toward 5% would push FMV toward the low-$30s

gaps: Statutory surplus is an estimated range (~$300-450M), making the premium-to-surplus figure a wide 3.3-5x band; a precise pull from the statutory (yellow-book) filings would tighten the leverage analysis — though this is constrained by disclosure timing.

True policy-level retention/persistency remains undisclosed and is therefore estimated (~70-80%) rather than observed; the thesis would be even stronger with cohort LTV/CAC data if Root ever discloses it.

The exact prior-year reserve-development figures, while specific and internally consistent, rest on the author's 10-K Item 8 citation that could not be re-pulled via the filing tool this review; a reproduced reconciliation table would be the final belt-and-suspenders.
